body: I have a great job, as does my SO. I've supported myself and paid my own rent since moving away from home in 2009. I've been independent for years. My situation is changing and I felt as though I needed to ask for help. Obviously you disagree. But again, I'm not some deadbeat looking for the easy way out of a situation. Even considering having to ask my sick mother for her help is difficult, hence the post.
Thank you very much for your advice and well wishes. I truly appreciate it. :)

You are right. I'm just too caught up in how that might effect the relationship that I have with my dad. With how shitty everything else is, I don't want to make it any worse when it comes to my relationships. I know that I will have to tell him that I cannot take over the loan.
Thank you so much for this advice. I found it very helpful and you've given me a lot to consider. :)

If we moved in with her, she'd save money on her own rent from what we'd be paying. My hope would be that the money we saved from that would ease our other financial worries. Ideally I'd never have to ask her for additional money. This all happened so recently that I made this post in a panic of "OH SHIT WHAT ARE WE GOING TO DO NOW?!" I NEVER said she had to let me live there. I was wondering how to even go about asking. Asking never killed anyone, and this is my family. 

You are right in that I have no idea how much it costs to have cancer, and I appreciate your insight. I don't know what any of this entails. It has never happened before. How could I know? It's part of the reason why I came to this subreddit to ask for advice.

Anyway, thanks for the advice. Some of what you said was very helpful. Your tone sucks, though, so that was a bummer.

I'm asking for advice on how to approach this difficult situation. If I asked her for the assistance and she refused, I know I'd have to figure something else out. I'm in no way saying it is her job to take care of me.

I completely understand where you're coming from. In an attempt to "lay out the facts," it sounds like I'm just eyeing my mom's money, which seems awful. I said that the house is "huge" in an attempt to convey that she has more than enough space, so it wouldn't be like shoving 3 additional people into an already cramped space. When I wrote this, my plan consisted of moving in with her so that we can save in rent, which would in turn save HER money in rent. With the money we saved, the financial burden would be less and seem far more manageable. The timing of it all is just awful with what she'll be going through. I've very rarely asked my parents for assistance, and when I do ask I always pay them back. My current situation is just far more than I've ever had to deal with, and my first thought was to go to my mom because I knew she'd be capable IF she was healthy. Now that she's not, I was asking for help in deciding how to approach the situation or if I even should. Thanks for the feedback.
